ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); system records show the driver never pressed "I'm Here" and never waited the required 3+ minutes after an arrival confirmation, so the no-show fee did not validly accrue.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat is a plain pickup/coordination exchange ("At the pickup point, silver Toyota Altis", "Waited 4 min, cancelling") — no threat, abuse, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, and the dispute type is no_show, not safety. No escalation on SAFE grounds.

Route of the dispute: cancelled_by = driver and the driver asserts a rider no-show, so NS-0 sends the case to NS-1 / NS-2. NS-1 requires all three: (i) the driver pressed "I'm Here" (or a platform automatic arrival confirmation), (ii) GPS placing the driver within 200 m of the pickup at that moment, and (iii) a continuous wait of more than 3 minutes within 200 m after the tap until cancellation. Requirement (i) fails outright: F6 records that driver_pressed_here_at is null — the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival. The driver's own statement concedes this ("I forgot to press the I'm Here button but I was there") [F12]. A driver's statement is a claim, not a system record, and cannot supply the missing arrival confirmation (the GPS/timeline records override it). Because (i) is not satisfied, NS-1 cannot be met and the $6.61 no-show fee is not validly established → NS-2: full refund of $6.61, refund_full.

For completeness, the physical-presence facts would otherwise have helped the driver: within 200 m the driver accumulated 5 min 20 s [F2], and he was stationary 4 min 0 s, 40 m from the pickup, immediately before cancelling [F3]. But NS-1 is conjunctive, and (i) is a hard precondition ("Drivers are only allowed to indicate arrival and impose the Waiting Time Fee only if he/she …"). Note also that the only "arrival" on the record is a platform-recorded approach (F5) — and F6 expressly rules out any platform automatic arrival confirmation, so (i) is not salvaged that way either. The fee is therefore refunded in full and issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7 (no cash).

Account flag: NS-2's flag_account is triggered only where the driver did press "I'm Here" while GPS showed him more than 200 m from the pickup. Here he never pressed the button at all (F6, F12), so that specific abuse condition is not met and no flag is applied. RD-6 does not apply (this is not an upheld route-deviation case); F17 (0 upheld disputes) would not support it in any event. The rider's profile [F16] is not relied upon — profiles cannot decide a case.

Evidence status: sufficient. The record settles every element needed — the cancellation event and its charge [F4, F7], and the decisive absence of an arrival confirmation [F6], confirmed by the driver's own written statement [F12]. No GPS gap relevant to the ruling was identified; the 3-minute / 200 m measurements are complete and do not affect the outcome because (i) already fails.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's statement that he 'was there' and that the rider no-showed is a claim, not consent- or arrival-evidence; system records (F6: driver_pressed_here_at null, no platform auto-arrival) override statements, and NS-1(i) requires an arrival confirmation that does not exist here.

The platform-recorded approach at 22:41:30 is an arrival-time marker, not an 'I'm Here' tap or automatic arrival confirmation; F6 expressly states no automatic arrival was recorded, so NS-1(i) remains unmet.
